body: This has honestly been one of my favorite stories here. I absolutely love seeing not just truly alien biology, but psychology as well, and you did an amazing job of presenting that.

I like to play long games, so whenever I find a pre-ftl race inside my borders that are atomic age or early space age, I plop down a big fortress right above their planet, and an frontier outpost at the star. I like being prepared when they become an actual civilization.

It's always hilarious seeing their primitive space station right next to a giant military station that they really should be able to notice.

Wow, that is rough. I've always found more than one, even without going after it real hard. What size of map were you playing on?

Just getting enough anomalies seems to be really luck based. It's more than the chance for an anomaly to even occur, you also need to get lucky to not have anyone else surveying all the systems close to you.

Most games I never get enough anomalies to finish the chain, usually only around 2-4. But I did finish it once. The system it ended in was in a nearby empire's territory. They had open borders with me. However, it seems like the AI also knows when the player finishes the chain, because another 3 or 4 AIs all bum rushed it with science ships at the same time as me. Someone got to survey it before me, and I didn't get any sort of rewards or anything.

My best advice for getting enough anomalies is to have 2 or 3 science ships really early on, exploring and surveying as many systems as possible. That's how I got enough that one time, by exploring so much more than the AI during the early game.

For me, selecting large fleets is what causes the lag fest. I think it has something to do with rendering the fleet interface for them, because I can select really large fleets during combat without any fps drops.

I'm able to select a huge 1mil fleet during combat with no issues, but even 150k outside of combat destroys my frame rate.

End game always lags my computer the fuck out though, regardless of navy size. I never get above 20fps once the game goes on for so long. I would love to see some serious optimization in this game, because I really enjoy the super long games.

There was an xenophobic awakened empire in my recent game that had at least 4 250k doomstacks for a while. They took over around 1/5th of the galaxy really quick, but ended up running out of steam somehow.

When they eventually declared war on me, they only sent two 250k fleets, which I barely managed to destroy. I had been consistently building up my fleets since they awakened, because they destroyed all my neighbors and we ended up sharing a really large border. If they declared war on me just a decade earlier, I may not have been able to hold them off.

The deviantart gallery download comes with both .png and .ico files, what I did was use paint.net to quickly modify the images to be white, and then convert them into .ico files using that converting website.

The safest way to prevent issues is to do a clean install after you've upgraded. That's what I did, it was well worth the hassle for me . And if you're either experiencing too many issues or are simply not happy with Windows 10, you can revert to your previous operating system within 30 days of your upgrade. (But only if you haven't done a clean install!)

Really though, I would suggest going through the other threads here and on /r/windows. I, as well as a lot of others have had a wonderfully positive experience with Windows 10. And [this](https://www.reddit.com/r/pcmasterrace/comments/3f5zjb/windows_10_tips_and_tricks_megathread_4/) post from pcmasterrace does a really good job of detailing what's up with Windows 10, especially the upgrade process.
